The fiscal-rule calibration search — fitness, instrument and debt-ratio trajectories

Eight seeds, 1,000 draws, zero accepted: the debt bound rejects every draw, so the incumbent never moves off its hot-seeded start

Author

LEEDS_MODEL — JUST2CE

Published

September 28, 2026

Written: 2026-09-28 · Read from: search_trail_sraffian_all-gdp-deflated_20260928-151722.csv (the most recent completed fiscal-rule trail) and its companion fitness_table_*.csv.

The result, in one line: 125 draws across the seed shown here, 0 accepted — and that is the point. The incumbent stayed at 0.4973 throughout, because the debt-bound hard filter rejected every draw even as the search found fitter configs.

4. Where the accepted draws landed

**No accepted draws.** Every draw was rejected by the debt bound, so there are no
accepted-parameter trajectories to plot. The search's best *evaluated* draw (fitness
~0.014) still had debt growth above g in both regions.

Why the incumbent is stuck

The fiscal rule is seeded at ψ = 0.05 against a debt target of 0.6, but the incumbent’s debt/VA is ~4.3, so θ_w^eff = θ_w + 0.05·(4.3 − 0.6) raises the wage-tax rate ~0.18 immediately — a large contraction that parks the fit at 0.4973 (vs ~0.010–0.046 the no-fiscal-rule taxes,propensities,rates seeds reached). Fitter draws exist (down to ~0.08), but the debt bound rejects them all, so the incumbent never moves.

Per-cell sim/target ratios are not in this report because the search logs only the scalar fitness per draw — the 24-cell model/target table (calib_fitness()$table) is computed but discarded each draw. Adding it is a one-line change in R/calibrate_random_search.R (write fx$table alongside the trail) followed by a re-run; that is the only way to show the ratio trajectory per draw rather than the single worst cell above.

Sources: R/calibrate_random_search.R (trail columns) · R/calibration_2026.R (calib_fitness returns the per-cell table) · output/calibration/search_trail_*.csv · output/calibration/fitness_table_*.csv.
